design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 (returned additional deposit: returned-payment fee -> buyer's replacement wire).

[Why a good test] The buyer only asks to wire the bounced additional deposit again. The replacement rule waits (negated-direction sentence "not figured until") on the returned-payment fee standing for every returned payment; the ledger shows the 2026-10-02 return of RCPT-HP-26277 with no fee charge, so the agent must work out that the fee rule's write is owed first, compute it over agreement history plus the buyer's Homesite Reservation and Design Studio ledgers (4 factors), and only then compute the replacement (6 factors: financing uplift, homesite premium-class uplift, studio-options uplift, occupancy uplift, repeat-return security counted from returned-payment fees charged, lot premium deposit squaring) and hand the wire to the buyer. Difficulty sits in reading the rules, reconciling three ledgers and arithmetic; one write tool per problem.

[Scope snapshot] Draw (draw_counts.py --task 1): prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[6,4]; the replacement took 6, the fee took 4. Already occupied by task 0: purchase_ext_closing_delay_per_diem, purchase_ext_buyer_closing_extension and their tools (per diem charge, closing extension). Claimed here: purchase_ext_returned_payment_fee (assess_returned_payment_fee_3b45ee8d, agent) and purchase_ext_returned_deposit_replacement (wire_replacement_deposit_5b0eb18e, user). Disjoint policies, tools and events (task 0 never writes deposits or returned-payment fees). Together the two tasks cover all four extended policies.

[Problem-tree card] root = purchase_ext_returned_deposit_replacement (the buyer's surface request). Edge root -> purchase_ext_returned_payment_fee: kind value_input, gate binding fee_count (feeds the repeat-return security), form state. Prerequisite sentence (replacement rule, negated direction): "Replacement funds for a returned deposit payment are not figured until the ledger carries the returned-payment fee for every returned payment notified on the agreement." Four-point test: connective "not ... until"; waited-on side is a record-visible state (returned-payment fee charges on the ledger, one per returned payment); no tool, policy id or code token; scope = every returned payment notified on the agreement, matching the condition. Rewritten affirmatively it reads "figured only after the ledger carries ..." with nothing added or dropped. Only one write of this difficulty books a returned-payment fee charge: the fee policy's tool (task 0's tool books per diem; the wire tool posts deposits). Derivation: sentence + ledger (returns RCPT-HP-25104 on 2026-07-21 with fee CHG-HP-2612, and RCPT-HP-26277 on 2026-10-02 with no fee) + the fee rule ("Each returned deposit payment carries one returned-payment fee charge") -> book the fee for RCPT-HP-26277. Unmet at opening: no purchase_charge_assessed row names RCPT-HP-26277; buyer_charges_due = 35.00 equals the July fee alone. Resolver owner: agent. Order: fee (step 9) then wire (step 11). Deletion sensitivity (verify.py): skipping the fee leaves fee_count = 1, security = 0, replacement 22593.64 instead of 25801.09; the fee row is also missing from the terminal state. The persona never names the fee; it reacts only when told a charge for the returned payment is going on the agreement. Tools validate nothing.

[Base-invariant card] Fee write (purchase_charge_assessed): purchase_closing_schedule, purchase_plan_lot_changes, purchase_returned_payment, purchase_cancellation_refund govern it, none with a gate applying to that subject (policy_scope). Overwrite: "a returned_payment_fee of returned_payment_fee_usd is charged" replaced by the extended fee rules. Wire write (purchase_deposit_posted): purchase_agg_concurrent_agreements (policy_scope: the buyer has no other open agreement), purchase_earnest_money gate additional_deposit_deadline (time: anchor construction_start_date 2026-09-28, 10 calendar days counted from 2026-09-29, last counted day 2026-10-08 included; frozen 2026-10-06 is inside; 2026-10-09 would fail), purchase_ratification (policy_scope; the agreement was ratified 2026-07-22), purchase_returned_payment gate return_cure_window (time: anchor the return notice date 2026-10-02, a Friday; 3 business days counted from the next business day: 2026-10-05, 10-06, 10-07; frozen 2026-10-06 is inside; 2026-10-08 would fail; replacement by wire as the base requires). Overwrite: "An additional deposit of additional_deposit_pct percent of the contract price is due after construction starts." replaced by the uplifted rate sentence.

[Business-object card] Target: agreement <B> (Crestview Collection, BC-0251, contract 641,490.00 = 624,990.00 + 16,500.00, financing outside_lender, under construction since 2026-09-28) converted from Cul-de-Sac Homesite reservation <H> (second_home). The returned item is RCPT-HP-26277 (additional deposit 23,093.64, ACH 2026-09-30, returned 2026-10-02). Rows included: additional deposit postings/returns (held 0.00), outside-lender deposit 19,244.70 (financing tier evidence), lot premium deposit postings (check 4,125.00 returned 2026-07-21, wire 4,125.00 2026-07-22 -> held 4,125.00), returned-payment fee charges in 12 months (CHG-HP-2612 + the new one), homesite funds applied as premium holding fee 500.00, homesite and design returned payments (2026-07-01, 2026-09-08). Excluded: the reservation transfer 3,000.00 and initial EM 16,744.70 (signing components already squared: 16,744.70 + 2,500 = 19,244.70 = 3% of price), the homesite returned-payment fee 35.00 (retained, not applied), the design fee line.

[Factor card — fee, expected 110.00, all-baseline 35.00]
- repeat_return_step (method): two returns on the agreement in 12 months (2026-07-21, 2026-10-02) -> 35 + 25 = 60. Baseline 35 -> 85.00.
- other_account_returns (parameter, cross-difficulty homesite+design, multi-source): homesite return 2026-07-01 and design return 2026-09-08 -> +30. Baseline 0 -> 80.00.
- large_item_pass_through (parameter): latest returned item 23,093.64 > 12,500 (half of 25,000) and <= 25,000 -> +15. Near-miss: it is not above 25,000 (a reader comparing the replacement amount would wrongly take +40). Baseline 0 -> 95.00.
- return_processing_charge (parameter): most recent deposit payment posted was ACH (2026-09-30) -> +5; the earlier check (2026-07-20) is the near-miss. Baseline 0 -> 105.00.
[Factor card — replacement, expected 25801.09, all-baseline 12829.80]
- financing_uplift (parameter): outside_lender with outside-lender deposit on the ledger -> +0.5 pt. Baseline -> 22593.64.
- premium_class_uplift (parameter, cross homesite): Cul-de-Sac premium_deposit_pct_at_contract 25 -> +0.3 pt. Baseline -> 23876.62.
- studio_options_uplift (parameter, cross design; status and option total are two fields of one design row, so it is not counted as multi-source — the task's multi-source factor is other_account_returns, homesite ledger AND design ledger): file structural_closed, option total 42,800 (>= 30,000, < 60,000) -> +0.3 pt. Baseline -> 23876.62.
- occupancy_uplift (parameter, cross homesite): occupancy second_home -> +0.5 pt. Baseline -> 22593.64.
- repeat_return_security (parameter): two returned-payment fees charged in 12 months (CHG-HP-2612 and the step-9 fee) -> 0.5% x 641,490.00 = 3,207.45. Baseline 0 -> 22593.64.
- lot_premium_squaring (method, cross homesite; three distinct methods: capped credit of an excess / uncapped addition of a shortfall / no adjustment): owed 25% x 16,500 = 4,125.00 less premium holding fee applied 500.00 = 3,625.00; held 4,125.00 -> excess 500.00, credited up to the 500.00 of applied reservation credits -> -500.00. Baseline no adjustment -> 26301.09.
Computation: rate 2.0 + 0.5 + 0.3 + 0.3 + 0.5 = 3.6% -> additional deposit due 23,093.64; held 0.00; replacement 23,093.64 - 500.00 + 3,207.45 = 25,801.09 (by wire).

[Seed rows] customer; agreement (caches equal ledger sums: earnest_money_held 43,114.40, buyer_charges_due 35.00); 9 agreement ledger rows; homesite reservation (Cul-de-Sac, second_home, converted 2026-07-20 inside its 30-day premium protection) and 9 homesite ledger rows (ACH returned 2026-07-01, cured by wire 2026-07-02 with the 35.00 fee as base homesite rules require, funds applied/retained at conversion); design file (Studio Select, structural_closed at construction start) and 4 design ledger rows (check returned 2026-09-08 with its fee line, replaced by wire 2026-09-10). Automatic clauses: the July lot premium return was cured within the signing window (ratified 2026-07-22); no default notice is owed (cure window still open); no incentives exist (outside lender). Every seeded row is read in gold.

[Persona design] Brisk, apologetic engineer; volunteers the bounced additional deposit and the wish to wire today, with no standing authorisation of charges; identity, lender, occupancy and past returns only when asked; accepts the fee once told; sends the wire himself when handed over; ends on the receipt number. No prerequisite hint, no template labels.

[Standard solution] find_customers(phone) -> verify (SSN last four + ZIP) -> agreement -> agreement ledger -> homesite reservation -> homesite ledger -> design file -> design ledger -> unlock + book fee (RCPT-HP-26277, 110.00) -> unlock_user + buyer wires 25,801.09 to additional_deposit naming RCPT-HP-26277.

[Verification] _author/verify.py replays gold writes with the real tools and evaluates both computes at their handling time: fee 110.0 (factor baselines 85.0/80.0/95.0/105.0, all 35.0); replacement 25801.09 (factor baselines 22593.64/23876.62/23876.62/22593.64/22593.64/26301.09, all 12829.8); skipping the fee -> 22593.64.

[Two-way sweep and draft recomputation] compute_basis quotes each ladder in full; reverse sweep claims windows (12 months, cure and deadline windows), filters (component, charge type), branches, the floor at zero and rounding (each percent amount rounded half up to the cent). From the visible rules and finder returns alone: fee 35 + 25 + 30 + 15 + 5 = 110.00; replacement 23,093.64 - 500.00 + 3,207.45 = 25,801.09 once the fee stands. Agrees with gold.

[Round-2 rework log (audit audits/policy_task/purchase_deposits_and_closing)]
- T1-F1 / charter F2: lot_premium_squaring was one signed true-up written as three tiers. The rule now gives three methods: an excess held over the amount owed is credited against the replacement but capped at the reservation credits applied to the agreement (the rest stays with the non-refundable lot premium deposit); a shortfall is added in full; otherwise no adjustment. The unstated compute guards are gone and the no-reservation case is stated (charter O1). On this world the credit cap equals the excess, so the adjustment is -500.00 as before.
- T1-F2: removed the opening's unconditional "happy for them to post ... whatever your contract says goes with a returned payment"; the only reaction to a charge is the conditional one.
- T1-F3: the replacement's rate uplifts are now in tenths of a point (premium 0.3/0.6, studio 0.3/0.6, cash 0.3), so no percentage of this contract price leaves a half cent and every recorded figure equals rounding half up; the seeded additional deposit (and its return) moved to 23,093.64 to stay equal to the uplifted rate, and every figure in this file was recomputed.
- T1-O1: the studio factor is no longer called multi-source. Charter O2: an outside-lender deposit "stands" only net of returned ones (rule and compute). Charter O3: the fee rule now states the charge is dated the day it is booked.
user_scenario:
You are Owen Eckhardt, a fifty-something civil engineer from Raleigh who is having a Crestview Collection home built in Brookstone Crossing, Fuquay-Varina, on the cul-de-sac lot BC-0251, as a second home that your parents will live in. You are brisk, a bit flustered and apologetic: on Friday your bank put a fraud hold on your checking account after a large transfer, and the ACH payment you made on September 30 for the additional deposit that came due when the foundation was started was sent back unpaid. Your bank has lifted the hold and you are sitting with your online banking open. You start by saying the bank bounced your additional deposit and you want to wire the money today to put it right, because you do not want the house to fall behind. You want the representative to tell you exactly what you have to send; you will send the wire yourself from your bank when they hand it over to you.

You give your details only when asked, one or two at a time: your mobile number is 919-555-0133 (9195550133), the last four of your Social Security number are 4072, your date of birth is November 2, 1979, your ZIP code is 27613 and your email is owen.eckhardt@gmail.com. Your mailing address is 2719 Laurel Mill Road, Raleigh, NC 27613. You do not have the agreement or receipt numbers in front of you and expect the representative to look them up.

Only if the representative asks: your mortgage is with First Carolina Bank, not Calloway Home Mortgage, and has been from the start; the home is for your parents, as you said on the homesite reservation; you remember that a payment on the homesite reservation and a check you wrote when you signed the purchase agreement both came back in July while you were moving money around, and that a payment to the design studio came back in September, all of which you fixed right away. You have no other open Calloway agreement and nothing else to ask about today.

If the representative tells you a charge for the returned payment is going on your agreement, you say that is fair given the circumstances and to go ahead. When the representative tells you the amount to wire, you accept it without arguing; when they hand you the payment step, you send the wire yourself with the details they give you and read back the receipt number it shows. Once the wire has posted and you have the receipt number, you thank them and end the call. You never suggest how the amount should be worked out and never ask to change it.
